issue.title: [Bug] list_directory leaks all hidden files/dotfiles by default due to !dirPath.startsWith('.')

steps:
Set up a small fixture in the workspace by running this exact shell command:
mkdir -p .git
n=zzhiddenmarker
printf 'MARKER=hidden-ok\n' > ".$n"
mkdir -p ".$n-dir"
printf 'x\n' > ".$n-dir/entry.txt"
printf 'ref: refs/heads/main\n' > .git/HEAD

When it finishes, just reply 'fixture ready' — don't describe the files.
Run the list_directory tool with default arguments (`{}`) on the current directory and show me the raw output.
expected: With `showHiddenFiles: false` (the default), a `list_directory` call whose path defaults to '.' must exclude every entry whose name starts with '.', so the returned listing must not contain the fixture dotfile/dotdir (`.zzhiddenmarker`, `.zzhiddenmarker-dir`) — per the issue's Expected Behavior and the tool's own 'skip hidden files unless showHiddenFiles is true' contract.
defect: `walkDirectory()`'s skip condition `!showHiddenFiles && item.name.startsWith('.') && !dirPath.startsWith('.')` is bypassed for the default path '.' (because '.'.startsWith('.') is true), so list_directory dumps all hidden files and directories (.env, .git, .zzhiddenmarker, …) into the output; fixed in 1.31.0 by PR #1253.

fault location.explanation: Contributing source location. See Root cause and the evidence review for observed behavior and limitations.

Root cause: The hidden-file skip condition additionally requires !dirPath.startsWith("."). For the default directory ".", that condition is false, disabling the hidden-entry filter. The retained default listing exposes .zzhiddenmarker and .zzhiddenmarker-dir. The absence of .git from that output does not negate the other hidden-entry leak.
